subject: Vulnerability management evidence & agreed scan cadence
messages:
From: Alice Bowman <alice@green-core.com>

Cc: security@green-core.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VM evidence for SOC2 SIG — scan cadence + SLA questions

Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our ongoing SIG intake and SOC 2 evidence collection we need a short package from Redwood covering your vulnerability management rhythm and remediation SLAs. Specifically can you provide the following: 

- A short statement of scan cadence (internal authenticated, external unauthenticated, container SCA) over the last 12 months
- SLA commitments for Critical and Important CVEs (acknowledgement window + remediation window) and what constitutes a compensating control
- How emergency hotpatches are handled (hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments) and any escrow/rollforward process
- Representative artifacts: one authenticated scan snapshot (last 30 days), an example remediation ticket with timeline, and a brief playbook excerpt

If you can include an attestation we can attach that to the SIG/CAIQ response. We'd like to share the artifacts with our internal auditors by May 20 — is that feasible?

Attachment: GreenCore_SIG_Request_20260511.pdf

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that helps.

Best,
Alice Bowman
Security Program Manager
GreenCore Finance
alice@green-core.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Bowman <alice@green-core.com>
Cc: security@green-core.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence for SOC2 SIG — scan cadence + SLA questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise package and I attached the playbook and a recent scan snapshot (see attachments). Short summary first, full details in attachments and the shared Drive link.

Summary (high level)
- Scan cadence: External unauthenticated network scans: weekly; Internal authenticated host scans: monthly; Container image SCA and dependency scanning: continuous on CI and daily for production registries; IaC static checks: per-PR with daily aggregate scans.
- SLA windows: Critical (CVSS >= 9 OR public exploit): acknowledgment within 24 hours; mitigation, patch deployment or compensating control within 14 calendar days. Important (CVSS 7.0-8.9): acknowledgement within 72 hours; remediation within 30 calendar days. We will declare exceptions with documented compensating controls when a patch is not available and provide a dated mitigation plan to the customer.
- Emergency hotpatch / escrow process: For Dedicated and Private customers we maintain an emergency hotpatch image and an escalation playbook; where a vendor patch is published that remediates a Critical issue we aim to stage and apply a hotpatch within 48 hours for Dedicated and Private deployments (operational/QA gating permitting). For Hosted API customers we apply protective WAF rules, routing fallbacks to patched model variants, and accelerated rollout windows; full kernel-level hotpatching in hosted environments is constrained by multi-tenant controls and we document compensating controls.

Deliverables (attached / drive)
- redwood-vm-playbook-2026Q1.pdf (playbook excerpt: triage matrix, SLA table, hotpatch checklist)
- scan-snapshot-20260501.csv (redacted authenticated host scan output — sample)
- hotpatch-escrow-procedure.docx (internal runbook summary; redacted)
- Shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/GreenCore/VM-evidence-summary-20260512

Evidence notes
- The attached scan snapshot is a single host-export with identifiers redacted as requested; we can provide a second sample scan and the remediation ticket export (Jira) after brief coord with the engineering owner — ETA for that artifact is 48 hours if you need it in the auditor packet.
- For third-party OSS vulnerabilities we distinguish: (a) dependencies where our CI can apply an automated update (we will remediate per SLA windows above), (b) vulnerabilities in vendor-managed infra (we coordinate with the vendor and provide timeline/resolution evidence). Our playbook includes the ownership matrix.

Proposed next steps
- I'll loop in Monica (engineering security ops) and Karthik (vuln triage owner) to confirm one remediation ticket export and a short attestation paragraph.
- Requested delivery for auditor: May 20 is tight but achievable if we lock artifacts today — can you confirm the auditor will accept a redacted remediation ticket?

Attachment stubs: redwood-vm-playbook-2026Q1.pdf (12 pages, redacted), scan-snapshot-20260501.csv (1 file), hotpatch-escrow-procedure.docx (6 pages)

Thanks — Naomi Feldman
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0189

Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence for SOC2 SIG — scan cadence + SLA questions

Looping in a couple operational clarifications so Alice/auditors have everything they asked for.

Naomi — quick notes for the remediation ticket export:
- We'll redact hostnames and IPs; the ticket will include timestamps: detection -> triage -> remediation steps -> close. Expect one sample export (JIRA-REM-4521-redacted.csv) by EOD Friday (2026-05-14).
- For the hotpatch escrow: our procedure doc explains the gating steps: QA smoke, canary push to a dedicated pool, rollback window, and a post-patch validation sweep. The 48-hour SLA for Dedicated/Private assumes no regressions in canary; if a regression is detected we escalate per the canary-runbook (this is noted in the doc).
- Compensating controls examples we typically provide: temporary firewall rules, request rate-limiting, and application-level input-sanitization rules — the auditors have accepted these historically as long as the mitigation plan has owner + ETA.

Karthik — please add the remediation ticket export and a 1–2 sentence attestation that we own the remediation for Redwood-managed components and will coordinate with customers for infra/vendor-managed items.

Monica Patel
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
